correctness.rationale: Each of the three shore-permutation incidence orbits has an explicit uniform geometric proof. In incident cases, the cover by two reverse-arc cones has intersection a graph with exact vertex, edge, and component counts; its suspension gives integral sphere wedges. In the disjoint case, every extra forward vertex is dominated by the correct reverse-arc vertex, and the six-vertex core is a tetrahedral S2 with an exterior attached path, giving S1 wedge S2. Standalone enumeration checks 27 small cases without replacing the proof.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of all exactly-two-reverse-arc perturbations of the two-source complete bipartite directed graph. It exhibits qualitatively different dimensions and the precise n=4 transition in incident cases, while the disjoint case has a uniform simple-homotopy plateau. These features give graph-incidence-sensitive topology beyond individual finite invariants.
